rePinnedNote: RE-PINNED and EXTENDED on 2026-10-10 (M60 kotlin fold), after the file had been written once from the ruling and the analyzer was made to agree. Writing it found a REAL defect rather than confirming the code: `findNameNode` scanned only DIRECT named children of a declaration, and a `property_declaration`'s children are `binding_pattern_kind` (the `val`/`var` word, a NAMED node in this grammar) plus `variable_declaration`, which holds the name — so every class-body property was anchored on the binding KEYWORD's column (5) instead of its name's (9). The `flagged` pin above was 5 when it was first written; it is 9 now because the analyzer changed, which is the opposite of a pin being bent to fit. The same file gained the receiver-extension shape for the same reason after `script/m14/lanes/jvm-rulings-mutants.mts` measured that removing the name read changes 7,126 symbol rows over 1,200 corpus files — the read is load-bearing, so it needed a pin that can fail.
rationale: M60 (2026-10-10). Both JVM-family rulings were ALREADY implemented in this lane, and the A/B measured that rather than assuming it: `script/m14/lanes/jvm-rulings-ab.mts` reports kotlin's constructor name census at 1,978 symbols / 1,852 distinct names / **0 named the literal `constructor`** over a 1,500-file slice of the 82,222-file kotlin corpora, and its declaration anchor is read from `findNameNode` (the kotlin grammar exposes NO `name` field — measured, 0 name-field nodes over kotlinx-coroutines's 1,039 files — so a field-based A/B is not even expressible here). What was MISSING was a pin that can fail: K2 below (drop the `findNameNode` read) survived the whole kotlin lane before this fixture existed. The fixture is the family's shape, matching scala/declaration-name-anchoring and java/declaration-lines-825, and it is the pin for the two shapes the analyzer's own comments name as the ones it was written for: a MEMBER behind an annotation and a doc comment, and a WRAPPED class header — `private data class SuspendedObject(` on 25 with `val transaction: Int` on 26 is Exposed SpringTransactionManager.kt's shape, where the class symbol claimed the parameter's line (measured 94 vs 93 there). The two forbid rows are that pre-fix behaviour, both recorded in this lane's own measurements: the class anchored on its parameter's line, and a secondary constructor anchored on its bare `constructor(` keyword line (9 such rows on Exposed ResultRow.kt/Table.kt/ColumnType.kt).
